=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd by Harbourglass Ventures
**Baseline:** AUD 24,000,000 | debt-free/cash-free | NSW law

**Overall view:** The Seller's package moves risk heavily onto us. It also tries to stop us reviewing most of it. The Disclosure Letter is fairly candid about seven live problems. The Seller Update then tries to deal with each one by:

- treating it as disclosed or known, so we cannot claim for it;
- capping it under the general regime; or
- leaving it until after Completion.

We should reject the framework and deal with each known issue through conditions, Completion deliverables, price deductions or specific indemnities.

I have only seen this cover document and the Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA, the clause wording, or DD-002 to DD-012. The points below need checking against those documents.

---

## 1. Threshold point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

**Issue.** The Seller has labelled almost every clause "[STANDARD]". It says these clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the limitation and disclosure frameworks have "already [been] accepted."

**Why it matters.** We have no record of agreeing any of this. The same email invites our "mark-up", which contradicts the claim. Every substantive risk point (fundamentals, disclosure, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident) sits under a [STANDARD] tag. If we accept the framing, we give up the review.

**Recommendation.**
- State in writing that no clause is agreed until the SPA is agreed as a whole.
- State that the labels have no status and that we have reviewed the full package.
- Make sure no "agreed positions" schedule or recital based on this note gets into the SPA.
- Please confirm internally that no one on our side has agreed these positions, even informally.

---

## 2. Limitations regime

### 2.1 Fundamental warranties subject to the general cap and 18-month limit. **Reject.**

Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Capping them at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window would leave us with a title defect worth AUD 24m and only 20% recovery. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that.

**Push for:**
- Title, capacity, authority and solvency warranties capped at 100% of the price.
- A claims period of at least 6 years. This matches the contract limitation period under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW). If the SPA is executed as a deed, the period is 12 years.
- No de minimis or basket for these warranties.

### 2.2 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13), with limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). **Reject.**

Combined, these clauses would pull the following under the 20% cap, the basket and the 18-month limit:
- the specific indemnities, including Ironquay;
- tax claims;
- covenant breaches;
- leakage and completion adjustments; and
- arguably fraud.

**Push for:** express carve-outs from all limitations for:
- fraud, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment;
- fundamental warranties;
- tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
- all specific indemnities, each with its own cap and period;
- pre-Completion covenants and restrictive covenants;
- price adjustments and debt/cash mechanics; and
- equitable relief (injunction and specific performance), which the exclusive-remedy clause must not exclude.

Non-reliance language has limited effect against claims for misleading conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. We should still resist it and carve out fraud expressly.

### 2.3 Cap, de minimis, basket and time limit

| Term | Seller | Comment | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Low end of market | 30–35%, or 20% only with W&I cover and an escrow |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | About 0.1%; workable | AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | About 1.04% of price; above typical range | About 0.5% (AUD 120k), **tipping** (recover from first dollar) |
| Time limit | 18 months | Within market | 24 months, covering two audit cycles |
| Tax | "Settled" | Not settled | Tax indemnity and warranties for at least 5 years, capped at price. ATO amendment periods are generally 4 years, and longer for fraud or evasion. |

If W&I insurance is being considered, note that it will exclude every matter in the Disclosure Letter. That makes the specific protections in section 4 essential.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2). **Reject.**

This would qualify every warranty by everything in DD-002 to DD-012, the Accounts, the statutory registers and any public record. That includes material we were never pointed to. The warranties would be largely empty.

**Push for:**
- Only matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify their nature, scope and financial effect.
- If any data room disclosure is conceded, limit it to an indexed, USB-archived data room annexed to the SPA, with no general deemed disclosure of public records.
- No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities.
- No updating disclosure between signing and Completion that cures breaches.

Paragraph 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable only if it cannot be used to argue that a specifically disclosed matter is immaterial.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3). **Reject. This is the most dangerous single clause.**

It excludes claims for anything we *or our advisers* knew, **or which was "discoverable"** from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge.

We now know about Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the incident and Sandbar. On this drafting, none of them could ever found a claim.

**Push for:**
- An express clause that buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, and due diligence do not affect any Claim, except to the extent a matter is fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- Fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals only. Never "discoverable", and never advisers.
- Because of the knowledge risk, every known issue must be dealt with through price, conditions, Completion deliverables or a specific indemnity, **not** warranties.

---

## 4. Specific issues

### 4.1 Bluefen consent (DD-002; cl 3/6.3)

**Facts.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (roughly 30%). It has a change-of-control consent right (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3). DL 2 confirms there is no consent yet and no evidence the conditions are met.

**Problem.**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is weak.
- Treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of "written consent" would allow a consent that is conditional, or that leaves the cl 11.3 conditions unmet.
- Losing this customer would undermine the valuation.

**Push for:**
- A condition precedent requiring *unconditional* written consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, and evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. This should include any changed terms, which the Buyer must approve.
- The condition to be waivable by the Buyer only.
- The Seller to use all reasonable endeavours, at its own cost.
- A sunset date with a Buyer walk right.
- No amendment to the Bluefen contract without Buyer consent.
- If the commercial team prefers, a price adjustment, escrow or earn-out linked to Bluefen retention or renewal.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (DD-003; cl 2/7)

**Facts.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. There is a change-of-control clause (cl 8.1) and a discharge clause (cl 9.2). Nothing has been repaid or discharged.

**Problem.**
- A release "following Completion" is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free.
- The change-of-control clause may trigger default or acceleration at Completion.
- We would own a company with live security over its assets, and possibly over the shares.

**Push for:**
- Treat the facility as Debt, deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark at Completion under a payoff letter, including break costs and interest to the payoff date.
- Completion deliverables:
  - an executed deed of release and discharge;
  - PPSR financing statement releases or undertakings to release under the *Personal Property Securities Act 2009* (Cth); and
  - return of any title documents.
- Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the Sale Shares. This also affects title (see 4.8).
- A specific indemnity for any residual facility liability.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005; funds flow)

**Problem.** The bonuses are described as "a matter for the Seller" but are left out of the funds flow. The Company is the employer, so the Company, and therefore we, will pay them. The amounts also attract on-costs:
- PAYG withholding;
- superannuation guarantee, likely, at 12%;
- NSW payroll tax at 5.45%; and
- workers' compensation premiums.

The continued-employment conditions mean some amounts will fall due after Completion, on our watch.

**Push for:**
- Bonuses and all employer on-costs treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from the price.
- Payment through payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from the deduction.
- Any amounts that fall due later held in escrow.
- A specific indemnity, outside the limitations.
- Confirmation that there are no other change-of-control or retention payments.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010; cl 11.1)

**Facts.** Ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials passes only when *every* SOW3 fee has been paid in cleared funds (DD-004 cl 7.3). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Problem.** The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it relies on, not the AUD 180k itself. The current indemnity covers only the payment. That leaves out:
- infringement claims;
- injunction risk;
- re-development cost; and
- customer claims if the product uses SOW3 materials.

**Push for:**
- Settlement of all SOW3 fees before Completion, at the Seller's cost, or a deduction from the price.
- Confirmation from Ironquay of payment in full.
- An executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable or condition, with moral rights consents where relevant.
- A broad specific indemnity for all Loss arising from Ironquay or SOW3 IP ownership or infringement. It should have a separate cap (up to the price, or at least a meaningful multiple), a period of at least 6 years, and sit outside the general limitations and knowledge exclusion.

### 4.5 Data export and privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6/Sch 6)

**Facts.** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 it was unknown whether anyone accessed the file or whether notification is required.

**Problem.**
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), an entity that suspects an eligible breach must take reasonable steps to complete its assessment within 30 days (s 26WH).
- More than 30 days have passed since 22 September. Either the assessment is complete and the Seller has not told us, or the Company may already be non-compliant.
- The Seller's assurance that the matter is "not expected to be material" has no evidential basis. Privacy penalty exposure has increased following the 2022 and 2024 amendments.
- Customer contract notification and security obligations may also have been triggered.

**Push for:**
- An immediate update covering the forensic findings, the NDB assessment outcome and date, any OAIC or individual notifications, and any customer notices.
- A pre-Completion covenant that the Company handles the incident properly and keeps us informed, with Buyer consultation rights.
- A specific indemnity covering:
  - regulatory penalties and investigation costs;
  - third-party and customer claims;
  - notification and remediation costs; and
  - credit monitoring.
- The indemnity should sit outside the cap, basket and knowledge exclusion, with a period of at least 3–4 years.
- Consider a retention amount until the matter is closed.
- Consider a Material Adverse Change (MAC) or walk right if the investigation shows a confirmed eligible breach with significant regulatory action.

### 4.6 Sandbar renewals of AUD 330,000 (DD-008, DD-011)

**Problem.** These are three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110,000 each. That pattern suggests a single commitment may have been split to stay under an approval threshold. It could be a conduct-of-business consent threshold, a material contract definition or an internal approval limit. The Disclosure Letter will not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The Seller's "ordinary-course" label is only an assertion.

**Push for:**
- Copies of all three contracts, plus dates, approvals, terms and termination rights.
- If the renewals were entered into after the accounts date, or are not ordinary course, treat them as Seller cost: through a price adjustment, as Debt to the extent prepaid or accrued, or as leakage.
- Aggregation language in the conduct-of-business covenants and material contract definitions, so that related contracts count together.
- A warranty that no contracts have been split to avoid thresholds.

### 4.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

The Seller offers its own reading that neither document requires consent to a share sale. We should rely on our own review.

**Push for:**
- Confirm whether the Mossvale "assignment" definition, or any deemed-assignment wording, captures a change in control.
- If it does, make Mossvale consent a condition.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable, or a Seller covenant to be met before Completion.
- Obtain a warranty that no counterparty consent is required for the transaction other than those listed.

### 4.8 Title (DD-012)

**Problem.** A share register held by the Seller is not enough evidence of title. DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified title.

**Push for:**
- Fundamental title warranties: legal and beneficial ownership, no Encumbrances, no options or rights over shares, and fully paid shares.
- An ASIC company extract and a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
- Original share certificates or a lost certificate indemnity, plus a signed share transfer.
- A history of the issued capital.
- Confirmation that Riverlark security does not attach to the shares, or releases at Completion if it does.

### 4.9 Tax and IP warranties: "settled under the general regime"

These are not settled.

- **Tax:** we need a separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses, with at least 5 years and a cap at the price.
- **IP:** the IP warranties should be fundamental-adjacent, given Ironquay, with a longer period and a higher cap.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "[STANDARD]"/"pre-cleared" framing in writing.** Nothing is agreed until everything is agreed.
2. **Fundamental warranties** (title, capacity): cap at 100% of price, at least 6 years, no thresholds.
3. **Carve-outs from all limitations:** fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price mechanics and equitable relief.
4. **General limitations:** 30–35% cap, tipping basket of about 0.5%, AUD 10–15k de minimis with aggregation, 24 months.
5. **Disclosure:** specific and fair disclosure only. No general disclosure of the data room or public records, and no curing disclosure before Completion.
6. **Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3):** delete. Due diligence and knowledge should not prejudice claims. Never "discoverable" knowledge.
7. **Bluefen:** unconditional, Buyer-approved consent as a condition waivable only by us, with a sunset date and walk right. Consider price protection.
8. **Riverlark:** repay from the price at Completion under a payoff letter. Deed of release and PPSR releases at Completion, not after.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus all on-costs treated as Debt, deducted from the price and paid through payroll, with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** fees paid before Completion and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable. A broad IP indemnity outside the limitations.
11. **DD-006 incident:** urgent update on the NDB assessment, given the 30-day period. Conduct covenant, specific indemnity outside the limitations, and a retention.
12. **Sandbar:** obtain the contracts. Seller bears any non-ordinary-course amount. Add aggregation in the covenants.
13. **Lease/Mossvale:** our own review, with consent as a condition if a change of control is caught.
14. **Title:** full warranties, ASIC and PPSR searches, certificates and a capital history.
15. **Security for claims:** an escrow or retention (for example 10% of price for 18–24 months). This matters more if W&I is used, since known matters will be excluded.

**Next steps:**
- Request the full SPA wording and DD-002 to DD-012 so we can confirm the points above.
- Request the incident update immediately.
- I can prepare the responsive mark-up and a short issues-list cover note to Seller's counsel.

### 4.5 Data export and privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6/Sch 6)

**Facts.** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 it was unknown whether anyone accessed the file or whether notification is required.

**Problem.**
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), an entity that suspects an eligible breach must take reasonable steps to complete its assessment within 30 days (s 26WH).
- More than 30 days have passed since 22 September. Either the assessment is complete and the Seller has not told us, or the Company may already be non-compliant.
- The Seller's assurance that the matter is "not expected to be material" has no evidential basis. Privacy penalty exposure has increased following the 2022 and 2024 amendments.
- Customer contract notification and security obligations may also have been triggered.

**Push for:**
- An immediate update covering the forensic findings, the NDB assessment outcome and date, any OAIC or individual notifications, and any customer notices.
- A pre-Completion covenant that the Company handles the incident properly and keeps us informed, with Buyer consultation rights.
- A specific indemnity covering:
  - regulatory penalties and investigation costs;
  - third-party and customer claims;
  - notification and remediation costs; and
  - credit monitoring.
- The indemnity should sit outside the cap, basket and knowledge exclusion, with a period of at least 3–4 years.
- Consider a retention amount until the matter is closed.
- Consider a Material Adverse Change (MAC) or walk right if the investigation shows a confirmed eligible breach with significant regulatory action.

**Problem.** These are three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110,000 each. That pattern suggests a single commitment may have been split to stay under an approval threshold. It could be a conduct-of-business consent threshold, a material contract definition or an internal approval limit. The Disclosure Letter will not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The Seller's "ordinary-course" label is only an assertion.

- A warranty that no contracts have been split to avoid thresholds.

### 4.9 Tax and IP warranties: "settled under the general regime"

These are not settled.

- **Tax:** we need a separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses, with at least 5 years and a cap at the price.
- **IP:** the IP warranties should be fundamental-adjacent, given Ironquay, with a longer period and a higher cap.

## 5. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "[STANDARD]"/"pre-cleared" framing in writing.** Nothing is agreed until everything is agreed.
2. **Fundamental warranties** (title, capacity): cap at 100% of price, at least 6 years, no thresholds.
3. **Carve-outs from all limitations:** fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price mechanics and equitable relief.
4. **General limitations:** 30–35% cap, tipping basket of about 0.5%, AUD 10–15k de minimis with aggregation, 24 months.
5. **Disclosure:** specific and fair disclosure only. No general disclosure of the data room or public records, and no curing disclosure before Completion.
6. **Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3):** delete. Due diligence and knowledge should not prejudice claims. Never "discoverable" knowledge.
7. **Bluefen:** unconditional, Buyer-approved consent as a condition waivable only by us, with a sunset date and walk right. Consider price protection.
8. **Riverlark:** repay from the price at Completion under a payoff letter. Deed of release and PPSR releases at Completion, not after.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus all on-costs treated as Debt, deducted from the price and paid through payroll, with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** fees paid before Completion and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable. A broad IP indemnity outside the limitations.
11. **DD-006 incident:** urgent update on the NDB assessment, given the 30-day period. Conduct covenant, specific indemnity outside the limitations, and a retention.
12. **Sandbar:** obtain the contracts. Seller bears any non-ordinary-course amount. Add aggregation in the covenants.
13. **Lease/Mossvale:** our own review, with consent as a condition if a change of control is caught.
14. **Title:** full warranties, ASIC and PPSR searches, certificates and a capital history.
15. **Security for claims:** an escrow or retention (for example 10% of price for 18–24 months). This matters more if W&I is used, since known matters will be excluded.
